solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knowing those swinging both ways bound to be high up in church

parts.note: an arch look is a knowing, sly one
bis is a slang plural for bisexuals, people said to swing both ways
to bound is to hop or leap

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a knowing, sexually fluid person destined for church preferment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' is a leap and 'to be' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bishop presiding over a province is among the highest-ranking clergy in the church.

clue.text: Water in a boggy place, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the bog word is used

parts.note: a quag is a quagmire, a boggy place

explanation.surface: Water lying in a marsh, for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for water, used in English in compounds and as a colour name.

clue.text: Arrive holding prize dessert dish

indicators.note: holding says the arriving word contains the prize word

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a pot is a prize or trophy

explanation.surface: A winner turns up clutching a prize pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed fruit in syrup served as a sweet course is a classic dessert.

clue.text: Husband and wife coping with tailing vehicle moving in the outback

indicators.note: tailing says the husband-and-wife pieces follow behind the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
hacking it means coping, managing

explanation.surface: A couple managing to tail a vehicle across Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The outback is the remote Australian interior; cutting through bush there is this.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing a way through wild scrubland is a way of travelling through the bush.

clue.text: Terribly artsy Romeo with many famous actors

indicators.note: terribly suggests something messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dismissive review: a pretentious Romeo, overloaded with celebrity actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast full of celebrities is star-studded, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Wartime operation ended by Kitchener, perhaps

parts.note: over means ended
Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal, an example of a peer

explanation.surface: A military campaign brought to a close by Kitchener.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener died in 1916, so he could never end this 1944 operation: 'ended by' is a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944 was code-named this, a Second World War operation.

clue.text: Unhappy about hard run

indicators.note: about signals that the word for unhappy is turned round

parts.note: unhappy means sad
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone miserable about a hard run they have to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a dash is a short fast run or sprint.

clue.text: Enduring bachelor involved in giving help

indicators.note: involved in says the bachelor letter goes inside the helping word

parts.note: aiding means giving help

explanation.surface: A long-lasting single man devoted to helping others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something lasting or permanent, as in an abiding memory.

clue.text: Order for copter to stop flying in German island

parts.note: heli is short for helicopter, as is copter
go is an order, a command to proceed
to land is to stop flying

explanation.surface: A command to a helicopter to come down on a German island.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a command addressed to the copter: 'Heli, go land!', which gives the pieces in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small North Sea archipelago belonging to Germany, ceded by Britain in 1890.

clue.text: Not captured outside Mons initially is correct

indicators.note: outside says the not-captured word sits around the other pieces

parts.note: untaken means not captured

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Mons

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A war report: Mons was not captured, and that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons is a Belgian town famous for a First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone who is not in error is right or correct.

clue.text: Philosopher works?

definitions.meaning: John Stuart ... was the English utilitarian philosopher

explanation.surface: A question about whether a thinker's output actually functions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names the Victorian thinker; the other is a factory or plant, as in steelworks or a cotton mill.

clue.text: Bank handsome victory on beach?

parts.note: good means handsome, as in good-looking or a handsome sum
a win is a victory
sands are a beach

explanation.surface: A bank wins a handsome victory, perhaps on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface financial bank is really a sandbank: a notorious one off the Kent coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shoal in the Strait of Dover where many ships have been wrecked, so a sandbank.

clue.text: Progressive splitting around in-patients' toilet?

indicators.note: around says the splitting word wraps the other two pieces

parts.note: forking means splitting into branches
a hospital ward is where in-patients stay
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A hospital lavatory is being divided up, which someone calls progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a progressive outlook is one that plans for and embraces the future.

clue.text: So to hers excitedly around nine in cowboy gear?

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters surround the Roman numeral
excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Thrilled, someone heads off to her place around nine dressed as a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' makes SSHOOTER from 'So to hers'; the Roman nine sits after its first S. The hyphenated gun name comes from its six chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolver with six chambers is part of a Wild West gunfighter's kit, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Showing due respect to Channel islands over hard water area

indicators.note: over in an across clue tells the solver to read the pieces backwards

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to, used before disagreeing with someone

explanation.surface: A deferential nod to the Channel Islands above a region with hard water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard water area' sounds like limescale country; it is frozen water, ice being hard water.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar sheet of frozen water covering a region is literally an area of hard (solid) water.

clue.text: For mine, aluminium is wastefully extravagant

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a dig is an excavation, like a mine
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A mining company spends wastefully on aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable's son squandered his inheritance, so the word means recklessly spendthrift.

clue.text: Stand across from top amusement park attraction

parts.note: best means top, supreme
a ride is an attraction at a fairground or amusement park

explanation.surface: Visitors queue for the leading attraction at a theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to stand with a leg on either side of it, across it.

clue.text: Diamond in box king left queen

parts.note: to spar is to box
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Card or chess play: a diamond in the box, a king left behind by the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a diamond is often called a rock or a glittering gem, something that flashes and glitters.

clue.text: Mean storm follows hail

indicators.note: follows says the storm word comes after the hail word

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a hail
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A weather report: a typical storm after a hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' reads as icy weather, but it is a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.

clue.text: Stone, plastic or zinc

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: A list of materials: stone, plastic or zinc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' reads as one more material in the list, but it is the anagram signal on 'or zinc'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a gemstone, a silicate mineral used in jewellery, so an example of a stone.

clue.text: Disadvantage with very good pen

parts.note: a con is a disadvantage, as in pros and cons
fine means very good

explanation.surface: A writer weighs up a drawback against an excellent pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen an animal is to shut it in, enclose or restrict it.

clue.text: One who's affected position over Europe

indicators.note: over in a down clue says position sits above Europe

parts.note: pos is the abbreviation for position

explanation.surface: Someone is influenced by a political stance on Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affected is pretentious, putting on airs, which is what a show-off is.

clue.text: Story by Scheherazade, perhaps, nearly a real treasure

indicators.note: nearly says the phrase stops short of its end, dropping the final words

parts.note: Scheherazade tells the tales of the Thousand and One Nights, so each is one of a thousand and one

explanation.surface: Praise for an Arabian Nights tale that almost counts as a true gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops 'and one' from 'one in a thousand and one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person who is exceptionally rare and valuable is described as being this, a real gem.

clue.text: Quick and effective line out of Dutch city

indicators.note: out of says the line letter is taken from the city

parts.note: Delft is a city in the Netherlands, famous for its pottery

explanation.surface: A swift, efficient exit along a line out of a Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone nimble and skilful works quickly and neatly.

clue.text: Some returned in carriage

indicators.note: returned says the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Some people came back in a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some returned in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no fragment fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle is a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Torch English home — note what then appears?

parts.note: to torch is to set fire to
in means at home
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: If you set an English house alight, notice what turns up next.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a building is set alight, the fire brigade's appliance is what then arrives.

clue.text: Part of film is material for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: real means material, physical

explanation.surface: A section of a film is a substantive thing for its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' fits the cinema scene but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A film was traditionally stored on spools, each spool holding one section of the picture.

clue.text: Republican leads top-secret rolling review

indicators.note: leads says the Republican abbreviation comes in front
rolling means tumbling about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A Republican heads a review of top-secret matters as it rolls on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: looking back over past events is a review of them, as in 'in hindsight'.
